Isolating the sixth-degree term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x-2)^{6}-1 & \ge 3 \\ 2(x-2)^{6} & \ge 4 \\ (x-2)^{6} & \ge 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the sixth root of both sides and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[6]{(x-2)^{6}} & \ge \sqrt[6]{2} \\ |x-2| & \ge \sqrt[6]{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
x-2\le -\sqrt[6]{2}\,\text{or}\,x-2\ge \sqrt[6]{2}
$$

So, the solution is

$$
x\le 2-\sqrt[6]{2}\,\text{or}\,x\ge 2+\sqrt[6]{2}.
$$
